rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this table pushes obfuscation strength up while retaining safety margin: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since arithmetic substitution is cheap and this Adobe-C++ benchmark is dominated by simple integer/loop arithmetic that substitutes well; BCF and FLA are raised substantially because the program's hot code is small unrolled loop kernels (largest functions only ~2KB) where control-flow flattening and bogus predicates yield high resistance, with RuntimeCost held near 0.55-0.60 to keep overhead acceptable on loop-heavy code; IBR is strong since indirect branching disrupts static CFG recovery and carries low size cost on these small functions; ICALL and IGV are enabled at moderate weights to obscure call targets and global references across the 292 template-instantiated functions without risking the correctness observed in round 1; SPLIT stays a supporting pass for diversity rather than strength; all CorrectnessRisk weights stay at or below 0.20 since the toolchain showed no fragility in round 1 but the cost dimensions are kept above 0.35 for the heavyweight passes to prevent runaway size growth beyond the 250KB reference text.
